questions.question: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its:
In E k = ½mv², the two 'dials' behave as follows:
options: Both mass and speed enter squared
Mass enters plainly (double mass, double energy); speed enters squared (double speed, four times the energy)
Mass enters squared; speed enters plainly

questions.question: A bakkie doing 15 m/s north and one doing 15 m/s south have:
options: Zero total energy because they cancel
Identical kinetic energies — squaring erases direction
Energies that depend on which is heavier

questions.question: Kinetic energy can never be negative because:
options: Negative numbers are not allowed in physics
The joule is defined as positive
Mass is positive and the squared velocity cannot go below zero

options: v² = 225 — the square on its own line

questions.question: Doubling the bakkie's speed from 15 to 30 m/s changes its energy from 90 000 J to:
Tripling a speed multiplies the kinetic energy by:

The wallet is handed to the road

options: Mass doubles the cash when doubled; speed QUADRUPLES it when doubled
Both double the cash when doubled
Speed only matters at high mass
Mass is squared in the formula

options: How quickly the same cash is spent — gently over distance versus instantly

questions.question: An object standing still has:
options: A wallet that depends on its height only
The same wallet as when moving
An empty wallet — zero kinetic energy

Yesterday's 4 kg paint tin lifted more than two kilometres straight up

They prevent the wallet from filling

options: Energy grows with the square of the speed, so extra pace costs more and more

options: Four times as severe — four collisions at 40 happening at once
